title.value: Mixed Patch Visible-Infrared Modality Agnostic Object Detection
title.justification: The title clearly states the focus of the paper is on modality agnostic detection using mixed patches from visible and infrared spectrums.
title.quote: Mixed Patch Visible-Infrared Modality Agnostic Object Detection

analysis.description: This paper introduces a novel training technique called MiPa that leverages RGB and IR modalities using a common transformer-based object detection vision encoder. The proposed method seeks to handle modality imbalance and enable efficient multimodal learning with a single modality inference. The paper demonstrates competitive results on RGB/IR benchmarks using this approach.

type.justification: The paper provides experimental results and comparative analysis with other methods on RGB/IR datasets to establish the effectiveness of their approach.
type.quote: Our work provides empirical results alongside a theoretical explanation based on information theory describing the benefits of using MiPa with transformer-based backbones.

name.justification: The research focuses on object detection and the integration of RGB and IR modalities, which is typically within the domain of Computer Vision.
name.quote: For instance, the combination of visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) has been shown to improve object detection tasks, which are part of computer vision applications.

name.justification: Utilizing both RGB and IR modalities to improve performance indicates the application of multimodal learning techniques.
name.quote: exploring patch-based architectures to build a powerful and yet simple training technique to create an RGB/IR modality agnostic vision encoder for object detection. Such approaches have been promising for multimodal learning.

name.justification: The paper deals with object detection specifically using RGB and IR data through a novel method.
name.quote: In real-world scenarios, using multiple modalities like visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) can greatly improve the performance of a predictive task such as Object Detection (OD).

name.justification: DINO is a transformer-based object detection model mentioned as one of the models used for evaluation.
name.quote: Furthermore, MiPa can simply be applied to different transformer-based detectors, such as DINO [46] and Deformable DETR [48].

is_contributed.justification: The paper uses DINO as part of their evaluation but it is not introduced as a novel model within this paper.
is_contributed.quote: Furthermore, MiPa can simply be applied to different transformer-based detectors, such as DINO [46] and Deformable DETR [48].

is_executed.justification: The paper discusses applying MiPa on DINO to achieve competitive results, indicating the actual execution of the model.
is_executed.quote: Implementation details. All our detectors were trained on an A100 NVIDIA GPU and were implemented using PyTorch.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares results obtained using DINO with other baselines and modeling strategies, discussing its performance.
is_compared.quote: MiPa demonstrates superior performance compared to using both modalities jointly and other baselines across different datasets.
